period: Prehistoric pigment extraction; later iron metallurgy
evidence: State heritage nomination distinguishes hematite/specularite ochre extraction from later iron-ore mining. Do not treat the earliest pigments as smelted iron.

period: Roman, first to early third centuries CE
evidence: Hydraulic washing of gold-bearing conglomerate documents a secondary source and a former landscape changed by mining. Heritage boundaries include tailings/infrastructure and are not an ore-body outline.
Mine, processing and transport remains document extraction; does not prove native silver as the mineral or Bronze-Age accessibility.
Long-lived mercury extraction documented by the heritage assessment. Exact source mineral/footprint requires geological record joining.
Historical mercury mining; keep separate from locations where mercury was used to process imported silver/gold.

period: Bronze and Iron Age underground salt extraction
evidence: Excavating museum reports salt under roughly 30m of salt-free cover; historical extraction does not mean surface halite. Earlier brine collection is plausible but not directly demonstrated there.
Historical rock-salt mining in a shared geological deposit; natural extent and accessible depth remain to be mapped.
Alum was manufactured from quarried shale by calcination and chemical processing. This is feedstock evidence, not a natural deposit of game alum crystals.
